title: The Sound Blaster mixer registers and DSP ports
covers: the mixer registers of the Sound Blaster series (CT1335, CT1345 and CT1745) and of the ESS AudioDrive, the DSP I/O ports and the EMU8000 bank ports, as Creative's hardware programming guide describes them and as DOSBox-X answers them

rows.text: Register 0x00 is the reset register.
Writing any 8-bit value to register 0x00 resets the mixer chip, and all the registers are then restored to their default values.
Register 0x00 is the reset register.
Writing any 8-bit value to register 0x00 resets the mixer, and all the registers are then restored to their default values.
Register 0x00 is the reset register.
Writing any 8-bit value to register 0x00 resets the mixer, and all the registers are then restored to their default values.
A write resets the mixer, but DOSBox-X sets the FM, CD, DAC and master volumes to 31, their maximum, not to the documented defaults.
A write resets the mixer, but DOSBox-X sets the FM, CD, DAC and master volumes to 31, their maximum, not to the documented defaults.
A write resets the mixer, but DOSBox-X sets the FM, CD, DAC and master volumes to 31, their maximum, not to the documented defaults.
Register 0x02 holds the master volume.
The volume is 3 bits: 0 to 7 gives about -46 dB to 0 dB in approximate 4 dB steps.
The default master volume is 4, about -11 dB.
After a reset the master volume is 31, its maximum, where the manual's default is 4, about -11 dB.
DOSBox-X takes 4 bits per channel for register 0x02, not the documented 3: a write of 0x07 reaches 15 of 31, not the maximum.
The mixer has two consecutive I/O ports, 2x4h and 2x5h, and 2x4h is the write-only address port.
On the Sound Blaster 16 the mixer register address port is at base plus 4 and is write only.
The index of the mixer register to access is written to the address port.
A read of the address port returns the index last written, though the manual calls the port write-only.
On an ESS AudioDrive, writing 0x40 as the mixer index resets the position in the ESS identification string.
On the Sound Blaster 16 the mixer data port is at base plus 5 and can be read or written.
The value of the selected mixer register is read from the data port.
The value written to the data port goes to the selected mixer register.
Port 2x6h is the DSP reset port and is written only.
A write of 1 and then 0 to 2x6h resets the DSP and returns it to its default state.
After the reset the DSP returns 0AAh at the read data port; if it does not, the card may not be installed or the address may be wrong.
A read of 2x6h returns 0FFh, though the manual calls the port write-only.
Register 0x08 holds the CD volume.
The volume is 3 bits: 0 to 7 gives about -46 dB to 0 dB in approximate 4 dB steps.
The default CD volume is 0, about -46 dB.
After a reset the CD volume is 31, its maximum, where the manual's default is 0, about -46 dB.
DOSBox-X takes 4 bits per channel for register 0x08, not the documented 3: a write of 0x07 reaches 15 of 31, not the maximum.
Port 2xAh returns in-bound DSP data and is read only.
Before the data is read in, bit 7 of the read-buffer status port must be checked to be sure data is there.
In-bound DSP data is read from the read data port.
The DSP's last output value is also stored by the Reveal SC400 command 0xE6 and at card start.
A read while the output buffer is empty returns the last value again.
Port 2xCh in the write direction sends commands or data to the DSP.
Before a byte is written to 2xCh, a read of the same port must show bit 7 clear.
DOSBox-X accepts the byte without checking the write-buffer status bit.
Port 2xEh is the read-buffer status port and is read only.
Bit 7 of the status port tells whether there is any in-bound data available for reading.
A read of 2xEh also acknowledges an 8-bit DMA or SB-MIDI interrupt.
The DSP output-buffer count is cleared by the Reveal SC400 command 0xE6 and by the flush, raised as data is added, and lowered on each byte read.
When the running program is DESERT or JUNGLE and the buffer is empty, a status read raises the output count, so bit 7 reports data that is not there.
Port 2xFh acknowledges a 16-bit DMA-mode digitized sound interrupt.
A read of 2xFh sends the interrupt acknowledgment to the DSP.

searched.gave: MAME's ISA Sound Blaster header cites no document; its mixer switch handles SB16 registers 0x22-0x3E, has no case 0x14 and no ESS AudioDrive.
The maker's ES688 data sheet (09/94) is https://www.alsa-project.org/files/pub/manuals/ess/688.pdf, a four-page scan whose OCR cannot be read line for line; esstech.com has no ES688 page.
No ESS ES688 datasheet: the components listing refused an automated request (HTTP 403) and a site search found no ESS page.
No item of its own: only Wayback copies of the same ALSA 688.pdf scan, which is the image-only document above.
datasheet4u.com lists ES688 as the same 380 KB four-page scan; datasheetarchive.com has no ES688 entry.

rows.text: Mixer register 0x14 is a case of the mixer write and read switches that only the ESS AudioDrive gives a body.
On an ESS AudioDrive a write to mixer register 0x14 sets the left voice volume from bits 7-4 and the right from bits 3-0, each widened to five bits.
On a card that is not an ESS AudioDrive the write to 0x14 has no effect: the case does nothing outside the ESS guard.
On an ESS AudioDrive a read of 0x14 returns the top four bits of each voice field, the left in bits 7-4 and the right in bits 3-0.
On a card that is not an ESS AudioDrive the 0x14 case breaks and the function returns 0.
On a Sound Blaster 2 the mixer register 0x0A writes the same left and right voice fields.
Register 0x22 holds the master volume, a field for the left channel and a field for the right.
Each field is 3 bits: 0 to 7 gives about -46 dB to 0 dB in approximate 4 dB steps.
The default value of each master volume field is 4, about -11 dB.
After a reset or a write to register 0x00 the master volume is 31, its maximum, not the documented default of 4.
DOSBox-X takes 4 bits per channel for register 0x22, not the documented 3: a write of 0x7F leaves one field at 15 of 31, not the maximum.
Register 0x26 holds the MIDI volume, a field for the left channel and a field for the right.
Register 0x26 is written with the left and right MIDI volume fields.
Register 0x28 holds the CD audio volume, a left and a right field.
Each field is 3 bits: 0 to 7 gives about -46 dB to 0 dB in approximate 4 dB steps.
The default CD audio volume is 0, about -46 dB.
After a reset the CD audio volume is 31, its maximum, where the manual's default is 0, about -46 dB.
DOSBox-X takes 4 bits per channel for register 0x28, not the documented 3: a write of 0x7F leaves one field at 15 of 31, not the maximum.
Register 0x2E holds the line-in volume, a left and a right field.
Register 0x2E is written with the left and right line-in volume fields.
Registers 0x30 and 0x31 hold the left and right master volume fields.
Each field is 5 bits: 0 to 31 gives -62 dB to 0 dB in 2 dB steps.
The default value of each master volume field is 24, about -14 dB.
After a reset both master volume fields are 31, their maximum, not the documented default of 24.
DOSBox-X takes the 5-bit field but attenuates 2 dB per step above level 10: the lowest eleven values are 1 dB short, so 0 is -61 dB, not -62 dB.
Registers 0x32 and 0x33 hold the left and right voice volume fields.
Registers 0x32 and 0x33 are written with the left and right voice volume fields.
On an ESS AudioDrive register 0x32 sets the master volume instead.
On an ESS AudioDrive a read of register 0x32 returns the master volume.
On a Sound Blaster 2 the voice volume is written by mixer register 0x0A into the same field.
Registers 0x34 and 0x35 hold the left and right MIDI volume fields.
Registers 0x34 and 0x35 are written with the left and right MIDI volume fields.
Registers 0x36 and 0x37 hold the left and right CD volume fields.
Each field is 5 bits: 0 to 31 gives -62 dB to 0 dB in 2 dB steps.
The default value of each CD volume field is 0, about -62 dB.
After a reset both CD volume fields are 31, their maximum, not the documented default of 0.
On an ESS AudioDrive register 0x36 sets the FM volume instead.
On an ESS AudioDrive a read of register 0x36 returns the FM volume.
DOSBox-X takes the 5-bit field but attenuates 2 dB per step above level 10: the lowest eleven values are 1 dB short, so 0 is -61 dB, not -62 dB.
Register 0x38 holds the left line-in volume field and register 0x39 the right.
Register 0x38 is written with the left line-in volume field.
On an ESS AudioDrive register 0x38 sets and returns the CD volume instead.
On an ESS AudioDrive the line volume register 0x3E writes the same left and right line fields.
Register 0x39 is the right line-in volume field of the mixer register map.
Register 0x39 is written with the right line-in volume field.
On a card that is not an SB16 a read of 0x39 returns 0x0A.
Register 0x3A holds the mixer's mic volume.
Register 0x3A is written with the mic volume field.
On a card that is not an SB16 a read of 0x3A returns 0x0A.
Register 0x3E holds the right input mixer switches for MIDI.L, MIDI.R, Line.L, Line.R, CD.L, CD.R and Mic.
Setting a switch's bit to 1 closes that switch, and 0 opens it.
The default is 0 0 0 1 0 1 1 for MIDI.L, MIDI.R, Line.L, Line.R, CD.L, CD.R and Mic.
For a mono recording of a stereo source the switches of registers 0x3D and 0x3E must be set to mix both channels into the left input mixer before sampling.
Writing 0x3E on an SB16 stores no switch: the case does nothing unless an ESS AudioDrive is selected.
A read of 0x3E on an SB16 returns 0, and on an ESS AudioDrive the line volume.
On an ESS AudioDrive register 0x3E sets the left and right line volume fields from bits 7-4 and 3-0.
Register 0x40 holds the right input gain field.
The gain field is 2 bits: 0 to 3 gives 0 dB to 18 dB in 6 dB steps.
The default input gain is 0, 0 dB.
DOSBox-X keeps no gain field at 0x40: it stores the whole byte and applies no gain, so values above 3 are read back unattenuated.
On an ESS AudioDrive a read of 0x40 returns the card's identification bytes one at a time, 0x0A for an ES688.
On a card with no ESS chip that is not an SB16 a read of 0x40 returns 0x0A.
Register 80h is the Interrupt Setup register, read and written like any other mixer register, that configures or determines the interrupt request line.
The byte from register 80h carries four interrupt fields, IRQ10, IRQ7, IRQ5 and IRQ2, and setting the corresponding bit to 1 selects the IRQ.
A read of register 80h determines the selected interrupt request line.
Only one IRQ bit may be set at a time.
On the PC-98 build the four bits select IRQ 3, 10, 12 and 5 instead.
On the PC-98 build a read returns the selected line's bit with the upper four bits set.
A ViBRA card ignores a write to 0x80.
A write first clears the selection to 0xFF, then the chain takes the first bit set, so IRQ2 wins over IRQ5, IRQ7 and IRQ10.
Register 81h is the DMA Setup register that configures or determines the DMA channels.
The byte from register 81h carries six DMA fields, DMA7, DMA6, DMA5, DMA3, DMA1 and DMA0.
A read of register 81h determines the selected DMA channels.
Only one 16-bit DMA bit (DMA5, DMA6 or DMA7) and one 8-bit DMA bit (DMA0, DMA1 or DMA3) may be set at a time.
To move 16-bit data through an 8-bit channel, all the 16-bit DMA bits are cleared and only an 8-bit channel is set.
An application should not write registers 80h and 81h to change the DMA and interrupt settings; only configuration software such as SBCONFIG.EXE should.
On the PC-98 build the bits select DMA channel 0 or 3, and the written byte is kept XORed with 0x14 for the read.
On the PC-98 build a read returns the channel bits together with the upper bits of the XORed byte.
A ViBRA card ignores a write to 0x81.
A write first clears both channels to 0xFF, then each chain takes the first bit set: DMA0 over DMA1 and DMA3, DMA5 over DMA6 and DMA7.
Register 82h is the Interrupt Status register, read like any other mixer register, that an ISR reads to tell whether an interrupt is its own or another's.
A bit of register 82h is set to 1 when the corresponding interrupt is triggered; the byte lists MPU-401, 16-bit DMA, 8-bit DMA and SB-MIDI.
Bits 0 and 1 follow the pending 8-bit and 16-bit interrupts, but bit 5 is set on every SB16 whether an MPU-401 interrupt occurred or not.
A write to register 82h stores nothing: the index reaches the default branch, which only logs it.
The card's FM music can also be accessed through I/O addresses 388h and 389h.
A write to 388h is a write to the FM music.
When the OPL mode is none, the write handler for 388h is installed.
The 388h write handler passes each write to the GUS AdLib register write.
The EMU8000 appears as one doubleword I/O port, two I/O ports that serve as a doubleword or two separate word ports, and two word-only ports.
The EMU8000 base port is the BLASTER E parameter, not always BLASTER plus 0x400.
Data0 is a doubleword port at BLASTER plus 0x400 for reading and writing doubleword data.
Doubleword data is read from Data0.
Doubleword data is written to Data0.
All I/O transactions must be word or doubleword; no byte I/O transactions are allowed.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte read and passes it to the chip's byte port.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte write and passes it to the chip's byte port.
The AWE32 code installs the read and write handlers at the base port for four consecutive ports.
Data1 is a word or doubleword port at BLASTER plus 0x800 for reading and writing data.
Data2 is a word port at BLASTER plus 0x802.
Word or doubleword data is read from Data1.
Word or doubleword data is written to Data1.
Data1 takes word and doubleword transactions.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte read and passes it to the chip's byte port.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte write and passes it to the chip's byte port.
The AWE32 code installs the same handlers at the base port plus 0x400 for four consecutive ports.
Data3 is a word port at BLASTER plus 0xC00 and the Pointer a word port at BLASTER plus 0xC02.
Word data is read from Data3.
Word data is written to Data3.
The pointer's low five bits are the channel number and bits 7-5 the register number.
After the pointer is set, the register is read or written at the Data port.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte read and passes it to the chip's byte port.
DOSBox-X accepts a byte write and passes it to the chip's byte port.
The AWE32 code installs the same handlers at the base port plus 0x800 for four consecutive ports.
